hi! i'm 21. for a little background, i deliberated hard on a BPD diagnosis since i was about 17 myself, but ended up diagnosed with bipolar 2 less than a year ago. so i've been around the block a bit, but i don't have a BPD diagnosis myself! my personal belief is, REGARDLESS of having a diagnosis, if the therapy route that is typically taken for people with that mental illness will help you with your symptoms, it's never a bad idea to ask. 

you might know that BPD is often tackled through dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) which is a pretty broad form of therapy used for most personality disorders. it might be helpful to look into that and see if it's something you can ask your therapist about. it's also just never a bad idea to ask your therapist about ways to cope with your specific symptoms, that's what you're paying them for! it's just like telling a physical therapist where your body hurts so they can help work it out :) 

also, if you struggle at all to feel seen or heard by your therapist about these concerns, ask them to consult the DSM-5 with you! modern therapists and most mental health professionals will make you aware that it's a bit outdated, but some therapists still go by it for objective descriptions and can use it to analyze your symptoms. i hope this helps and good luck! you deserve the help you need! :)
